findings.evidence: write_extension_binding validates bridge_bootstrap bytes and an executable bit at controller_deployment.py:94-100, but serializes only its path in bridge.command. ASSET_KEYS has no bridge_bootstrap, and _prepare_frontend_deployment at 116-145 accepts any absolute bridge.command without reopening or matching an approved bootstrap. An independent synthetic probe used the real helper, replaced the bootstrap bytes afterward (c663f8... -> 7eff4b...), and write_frontend_deployment still accepted it with no bootstrap seal.
findings.impact: The extension can execute different bytes from those checked by the root producer. Neither frontend deployment nor process configuration can detect the replacement.
findings.required: Bind bootstrap path, SHA-256, byte count, mtime ceiling, private owner/mode, and executable status in the immutable binding/deployment schema. Reopen and compare it during frontend and process production. The bridge command must equal that sealed path.
findings.title: The executable bridge bootstrap is discarded from durable asset provenance

findings.evidence: write_process_config revalidates deployment/assets at lines 198-207, then independently calls capture_path_identity while constructing RunControllerConfig at 209-215. It never compares the new PathIdentity to the frontend deployment seal or the supplied process_exec FileBinding. A bounded race probe changed controller_main only after its last _data read; process production succeeded and emitted frontend_identity SHA 9951b6... while the validated deployment still bound aeace2....
findings.impact: A replacement during the read-to-capture window is legitimized in the process config instead of rejected. The controller can execute a frontend not authorized by the deployment it was meant to enforce.
findings.required: Derive process identities from an atomic reopen and require equality with the already validated deployment/FileBinding path, hash, bytes, and mtime bound. Also bind the exact frontend deployment bytes parsed; never accept a later recapture as new authority. Add deterministic mutation-between-read-and-capture regressions for controller_main, deployment, node, and process_exec.
findings.title: Process production can re-seal a changed frontend executable after validation

findings.evidence: Frontend preparation only requires deployment to be somewhere below artifact_root (lines 151-155); it does not exclude empty session_dir/temporary_dir. Writing deployment into temporary_dir succeeds after sealing it must_be_empty=true and immediately fails _revalidate_frontend_deployment. Process production only excludes artifact_root and descendants (line 202); writing process.json into profile succeeds, adds a forbidden profile entry, and immediately invalidates the frontend deployment. Both behaviors were reproduced on exact synthetic copies.
findings.impact: A producer can return a FileBinding for configuration that its own strict revalidator rejects immediately, before any controller starts.
findings.required: Before any publication, reject output equal to or under a directory whose seal/public profile policy the write would change. Frontend deployment must not be in session/tmp; process config must not be in artifact/session/tmp/profile/cwd. Add post-publication revalidation assertions.
findings.title: Output paths can mutate directories whose just-written seals require a different state

mutable_dependency_record.assessment: The full dependency changed during review due separately owned work. The two imported helpers are byte-identical at the stated function hashes. Tests and probes used the held full hash; unrelated new DA001 code was not inspected or reviewed.

preserved_closure: The actual-red directory replacement regression is closed on the reviewed hashes. Existing exact schema, settings, fixed eight-key environment, directory identity, file hash, O_EXCL publication, and no-credential-read controls pass. These controls do not close A2CD-I1-I3.

scope.excluded: DA001 bootstrap implementation and changing process driver/completion sources were not reviewed. Bridge A2BR-I1-I6 closure was not reopened.
scope.execution: Exact temporary copies under approved Python 3.11; synthetic files only. No real bootstrap, main, controller, ORX, Docker, auth contents, task data, model, provider, or P0.

verdict: NOT ADMITTED. A2CD-I1 and I2 break executable/asset provenance; A2CD-I3 permits immediately stale self-produced configurations. No actual P0 or live controller activity occurred.
verified_negative_controls: Static controller_main byte tampering before process production was rejected and published no process config.
An unexpected frontend top-level field was rejected.
Injecting HOME into the exact child environment was rejected.
The six source tests reject unknown assets, enabled retries, stale nonempty session/tmp, replacement profile inode, process config under artifact_root, and overwrite.
The synthetic auth.json contents were guarded against os.open; the producer only enumerated profile names/metadata. No real credential file was accessed.
